_comment: The single source of truth for the agent-control socket protocol (docs/design-agent-control.md).
Two implementations read this file: src-tauri/src/control_socket (cargo test, via include_str!)
parses the requests and must produce responses of the shapes below; src/mcp/controlClient.ts
(Vitest) builds the requests and validates every response against the same shapes, and the
TS mock socket server answers with these responses. Add a case here before changing either side.
Supervisor scope (ADR 0004): callerScope says which caller may use which method and what a supervisor caller is refused; additionalResponses holds the further valid answers a method can give.

_comment: Who is asking decides what a request may do. Rust learns the caller from the peer PID: it walks the
parent chain and returns the first running IDE agent it meets, with that agent's role. No agent in the
chain: external. A supervisor: supervisor. Any other agent: worker, refused at admission. A PID that
cannot be read is refused like a worker (fail closed). Scope checks run in the dispatcher, after the
request has parsed, so an unparseable request is still invalid_request / invalid_params first.

supervisor.modelChoice: provider and model may be left out. Without provider, the project's balancing.next is taken, else the supervisor's own provider when the project allows it, else the first one it allows. Without model, the smallest ranked model the policy allows for that provider is taken (supervisorPolicy.fixtures.json modelChoice); none ranked is supervisor_denied (no_ranked_model). A resolved model of rank >= reasonRequiredFromRank needs a non-blank modelReason, else supervisor_denied (model_reason_required) naming the smaller allowed models. A spawn that goes ahead is appended to <app_data_dir>/supervisor-spawns.jsonl with its model, rank, modelReason and whether the model was picked by default.
supervisor.listProjectsShape: A supervisor's list_projects carries a top-level catalog { provider: [{ id, label, rank, useFor?, relativeCost? }] } with each model the listed projects allow, described once. Inside a project, the supervisor block's keys are sorted, so balancing precedes providers; providers[].permissionMode is left out for the provider's own default and providers[].models is "all" (every catalog model of that provider) or the allowed ids. params.project (a path or a project name) keeps only matching projects; none is unknown_project. The MCP server sends the result as compact JSON.
supervisor.spawnPolicy: supervisorPolicy.fixtures.json checkSpawn; refusal is supervisor_denied with its reason
supervisor.worktrees: spawn may pass worktree: true; remove_worktree removes an own child's worktree only when it holds no uncommitted change and no unmerged commit, otherwise answers removed: false and leaves it for a person. No path and no force are accepted: the folder is the child's own working directory.
supervisor.typing: send_input reaches its own interactive children only, like read_output and kill. It can answer a child's question or permission prompt, so the launch prompt tells the supervisor which ones it may answer and which go to the human. A headless child still refuses it (headless_no_stdin).
supervisor.linkPolicy: link_policy_get reads the supervisor link policy (stored, effective with origins, pending proposals). link_policy_propose stores a pending proposal and raises an inbox ask with Apply and Discard; nothing changes until a person presses Apply in the IDE. No socket method decides a proposal. External callers, and so the supervisor link socket, are refused both (supervisorLink.fixtures.json, proposals).
supervisor.finishedChildren: list_agents lists its live children and its finished ones while their result is kept (runResultsKept), each finished one with status idle or error, so an empty list means it started nothing, never that its agents were lost. dismiss clears a finished own child from the IDE and forgets its kept result; a running or queued one is refused (invalid_params).
supervisor.pingback: When a child finishes, Rust types one notice into the running interactive supervisor's console (bracketed paste plus Enter, the send_input path). Finishes are batched: the notice goes out once no further child has finished for pingbackQuietMs, or pingbackMaxDelayMs after the first one at the latest. It names each agent by id, name and status and says the notice comes from the IDE. A headless or finished supervisor gets none. While the human has a message half typed in the supervisor's console (printable keystrokes since the last Enter or Ctrl-C, the last one less than pingbackDraftHoldMs ago) the notice waits, and what finishes meanwhile joins it.
